items.stem: Which of the following data sets has the greatest standard deviation?
items.explanation: For the third data set, the mean is 4, and every value is 3 units from the mean, so its standard deviation is 3. Although the second data set has the largest range, most of its values are concentrated at 4, so its standard deviation is less than 3. The first and fourth sets have even less spread around their means. Therefore, the third data set has the greatest standard deviation.

The first and fourth sets have even less spread around their means. Therefore, the third data set has the greatest standard deviation.

items.stem: The numbers in a data set are 17, 4, 12, 8, 25, 12, and 27. What is the value of the mean of the numbers minus the median of the numbers?
items.explanation: In order, the numbers are 4, 8, 12, 12, 17, 25, and 27, so the median is 12. Their sum is 105, so the mean is 105/7 = 15. Therefore, the mean minus the median is 15 - 12 = 3.
items.pattern: compare mean and median of a set

items.stem: The numbers 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, and 21 are the values in a data set. A number x is added to the data set. If the mean of the resulting data set is equal to its median, what is the value of x?

items.explanation: The original sum is 99, and the remaining sum is 8(10.125)=81, so the removed value is 18. The original median is 11, while the new median is (8+11)/2=9.5; therefore I and II are true. The range remains 21-2=19, so III is false.

items.explanation: The original range is 17-6=11, so the new range is 22. Since the new value is the maximum, it satisfies x-6=22, giving x=28. The new mean is (62+28)/7=12.857..., or 12.9 to the nearest tenth.
